syntaxe: instruction_commune + deux sauts de ligne + instruction_du_plan + deux sauts de ligne + rappel_de_continuite
instruction_commune: Use case: historical-scene, a single complete cinematic epilogue for the French historical game Les Colons de Hotspring. Very wide landscape 16:9 film frame; high detail 1920 × 1080 or larger. Naturalistic frontier narrative painting with the convincing light and microtexture of a historical location photograph, subtly tactile grain, earth pigment and muted straw, warm pale wood, blue-gray shadow. American inland frontier in the later nineteenth century, a mature but modest wooden town in the same Hotspring valley. Behind the roofs, if visible, low elongated ochre striated hills, an eroded pale terrace, a low indigo ridge and a long saddle toward the centre; no mountain spires. Willow and cottonwood, no desert cacti. Ordinary inhabited buildings with believable modest footprints, horizontal timber plank fronts, intermittent covered boardwalks; Main Street follows the contour obliquely with houses to either side. Independent complete camera exposure, real perspective, figures and wheels properly grounded and scaled. Leave critical heads, hands, silhouettes and architectural edges clear of top and bottom six percent for the final 16:9 export. No painted words, readable signage, lettering, titles or game interface; no collages, inset panels, frames, logos or watermarks. All architecture generic except what the specific shot explicitly calls for. Never show church or belltower, bank, school, saloon, hospital, jail, railway, locomotive, tracks, station, oil rig, minehead, water tower, modern machinery, electricity, motor vehicles, flags or modern dress. No disasters or signs of a specific crisis, no guns, no stock western costumes or staged line-up. The town's height in relation to the river must be impossible to determine, to work for either approved foundation site.

instruction_du_plan.fin-equilibre: One long, unhurried look across the inhabited centre from a modest upper-floor window, the camera looking slightly down across a dense patchwork of low timber roofs toward the bend in Main Street. Mid-morning after soft intermittent cloud; some warm light catches the roofs and a line of trees. At the bend, a few families are talking, a repairer is mending a handcart, and residents share two baskets of everyday goods. Interwoven upkeep, livelihoods and unhurried human rhythms. Dignified realism, an established place in good working order; not a lavish city, no grand public building or fair. Allow the eye to travel through three convincing planes without making this an aerial map. Keep river and site edges completely out of frame.
instruction_du_plan.fin-industrie: View from a rocky wooded bank beside a working nineteenth-century steam sawmill. Foreground: substantial debarked logs, river coiling around a rough timber landing and reflecting a silvery sky. Middle frame: one distinct but low single-purpose steam sawmill with an open lumber shed, an attached saw house and one modest boiler exhaust chimney (not a headframe). A hint of visible steady steam against soft side light. Crews shifting sawn timber by hand onto a broad cart, tall orderly lumber stacks, mill workers' plain cottages. Turbid amber water, silt, felled banks and an edge of denuded pale woodland give industrial prosperity its cost. Compose a strongly graphic diagonal of logs and timber against the far slope in hazy late sun. The settlement beyond is only a layer of indistinct roofs peeking through steam, without indicating whether its centre sits on the lowland or on a plateau. Never show a train, railroad, mine, factory complex, pollution catastrophe, fire, crane or dam. Single small steam sawmill and local nineteenth century way of working.
instruction_du_plan.fin-commerce: At wagon-bed height at the mouth of a narrow wooden warehouse court, an immersive early market morning opens diagonally onto an already established Main Street. A broad oxblood-painted freight wagon at the far left or right, a pair of well-proportioned draft horses, an open tailgate with neatly tied sacks, unmarked covered crates and bolts of calico. Small teams of porters unloading them and two buyers conferring. An assortment of ordinary shopfronts and plain canvas awnings leads away into the lively middle distance. Clear ordinary faces and discrete gestures, not a posed tableau. Rich and active, not ostentatious. Keep river and site edges outside the frame. Bright, cool midmorning sun with warm reflected amber from the boardwalk, eye drawn between carts and inhabited rooflines. The route and method of trade is only road wagons; no special building, rail or bank.
instruction_du_plan.fin-ressources: A quiet view taken from the edge of a shared productive kitchen garden inside the inhabited town, long shadows in cool late-summer morning. Low wooden fencing, flowering native plants, healthy cottonwood and willow spreading over an unpaved lane, a spring-fed wooden hand bucket under a tree (no fountain or civic installation). In oblique middle distance, a long, layered row of modest lived-in plank houses with tended gardens, a woman and another resident moving baskets of vegetables, a few children at ordinary chores. The country is not empty: a mature green town quietly lives within it. In the background an opening in the canopy reveals blue hills and a hint of valley air, never the town's position above a river. No specialized public institution, water tower, dam, pump, dedicated civic park or institutional buildings. Painterly daylight filtered through leaves, quiet near foreground and warmly luminous roofs, a little wild ochre grass and natural dust, credible frontier ecology.
instruction_du_plan.fin-tensions: Standing under an unmarked shop arcade at blue hour, we look obliquely across a compact prosperous commercial street. Teeming crates and expensive folded bolts of fabric are being hurried inside, the afternoon's loaded wagons wait in the road. Two residents urgently draw heavy wooden shutters on one side while wary, separate groups regard one another across the street, holding back. A mother quietly takes a child's hand and steps into a doorway, more visible faces turn to follow the argument. Expensive goods and material activity are abundant but the open street has become intimidating; the image must tell both facts immediately without slogans. Slate-blue falling light, narrow bands of warm oil-lamp light restricted to ordinary store windows, dust and sharp near silhouettes. Keep all settlement topography off-screen. No gun, wounds, burning building, panic, barricade, law office or specific disaster; everything structurally intact. Human tension seen through postures and distance. No signs over the street.
instruction_du_plan.fin-declin: At the far end of an established Main Street in overcast early spring, an intimate wide low-angle shot looks diagonally along a long bank of aged timber porch posts and closed ordinary shops. Peeling paint, two empty worn loading platforms and most weathered shutters closed; a few intact windows have plain boards, patchy grass returns along the ruts. One small family and a second resident pack a few household bundles on an ordinary partly loaded horse cart, leaving broad stretches of empty street. A distant man sitting on a porch, roofs of homes and modest businesses receding behind them. The roofs are whole, the settlement still exists. Lower raking light under a low cool cloud deck, sparse muted earth and sage palette. A dignified but unmistakable economic and demographic retreat. Do not depict a fire, flood, epidemics, violence, ecological wasteland, broken industrial machinery or an identifiable failed business. Foundation altitude and river hidden by the street and façades. The gaze passes from close empty thresholds to the few vulnerable residents, leaving hopeful traces of life.
instruction_du_plan.fin-civique: A packed but orderly residential courtyard at the crossing of two side lanes of Main Street, in an established working-class timber town, circa 1891. Camera just above the last tread of a stoop at the edge of the crossing, a recognizable neighbour's-eye view, not a town vista or distant bland elevated view. Late autumn, muted pale earth, close rows of small modest rooms and houses with peaked timber roofs, visible backyard clotheslines, worn shared plank walkway, a repair neatly patched on the wall, baskets of simple food. At the clear centre, an older woman on a bench receives a small warm meal from a second woman with a cooking pot. A few steps back a carpenter kneels holding a loose board while another resident passes him a hammer to fix a shared step. Neighbours naturally encounter one another in small distinct groups in the lanes between the many inhabited modest homes, adults and children carrying small firewood bundles. Visibly close, crowded and cared-for, safe to move around, dignity and mutual aid rather than expensive prosperity, no posing for a group portrait, silhouettes readable even from the back of a lecture theatre. A broad patch of soft warm sun breaks into the muted, pale early afternoon light, illuminating the central exchange of food and the line of the homes. Keep aspect wide with strong skyline and roofs, believable anatomy, and separate gestures. The subject is the residents and their civic life, not buying and selling or a frontier tourist market. No sale stands, carts of goods, market awnings, commercial showpieces, military equipment, triomphe arch, recognizable institution or public building; no ragged destitution, weapons, extreme overcrowding, disease, or violence. No ground-level river or view exposing the town's foundation altitude. One coherent, whole, realistic nineteenth-century shot.

rappel_de_continuite: Match the series bible: mature town late 1880s–1893, pale willow wood and sun from camera left when visible; Black Ridge is low and dark at the far right, with a lowered central saddle. Keep foundation cliffs and river off-screen for all street or interior-court shots. The industrial riverbank is a separate working location. Each image stands alone as one full cinematic 16:9 composition.
